title: Emit index-change events so downstream caches can invalidate
body:
## Problem

When querystore upserts or deletes documents (via AOP bridge, bootstrap, or direct service calls), downstream consumers have no way to know a patient's indexed state changed. The `AfterCommitDispatcher` runs the write but does not publish an event.

## Use case (chartsearchai)

chartsearchai maintains two caches downstream of the index:

- `ChartCache` — a per-patient cache of the assembled chart context
- The answer cache in `ChartSearchServiceRouter` — caches LLM answers keyed on patient + question

Today both are invalidated by `ChartCacheInvalidator.invalidate(patient)` called from each AOP advice (`PatientDataIndexingAdvice.java:82`, etc). After migration, the writes move into querystore's `AfterCommitDispatcher` and chartsearchai loses the hook — caches will serve stale answers.

The current port-map doc dismisses `ChartCache` as 'orthogonal' to querystore, which is true for storage but false for cache freshness: the cache lives downstream of querystore writes and needs to know when they happen.

## Proposed API

Publish a Spring `ApplicationEvent` (or equivalent) from `AfterCommitDispatcher` after each successful commit:

```java
class QueryStoreIndexChangedEvent {
    String patientUuid;
    Set<String> resourceTypes;
    ChangeType type; // UPSERT, DELETE, BULK_DELETE
}
```

Consumers subscribe via `@EventListener` and react idempotently. The event must fire after commit, not within the transaction.

## Size

Medium. Event class, dispatcher hook, documentation, and a sample listener in the migration guide.

## Blocking

Soft blocker — chartsearchai can technically migrate without this if it accepts stale chart/answer caches until the cache TTL expires, but that is a real UX regression and arguably a correctness bug for users who edit obs and immediately re-query.

title: On-demand per-patient bootstrap (ensureIndexed)
body:
## Problem

querystore's `BootstrapService` does admin-triggered batch backfill. After that, AOP bridge advice keeps the index fresh on writes. But there is no per-patient lazy-initialization path: a first-touch query on a never-indexed patient returns empty rather than triggering an indexing job.

## Use case (chartsearchai)

The demo deployment at `chartsearchai.openmrs.org` has no batch job and limited resources — it relies on chartsearchai's `LuceneIndexer.hasIndex(patient)` probe (see `HybridRetriever.java:62-73`) to trigger per-patient indexing the first time someone queries that patient's chart. Without that, every freshly-installed deployment serves empty answers until an admin remembers to run a full backfill.

## Proposed API

Add to `QueryStoreService`:

```java
void ensureIndexed(String patientUuid);
```

Idempotent. If the patient already has any indexed docs, no-op. Otherwise, synchronously (or with a `CompletableFuture<Void>` variant) project the patient's clinical record into the store using the configured serializers and embedding provider.

## Size

Small to medium. Re-uses `BootstrapService`'s per-patient projection path; new service method, a 'has any docs for patient' check, and a thread-safety story for concurrent first-touch on the same patient.

## Workaround

chartsearchai can document that deployments must run a backfill before queries return useful results — but that breaks the zero-config demo experience and is worth fixing in querystore itself.

title: Service-layer search filters: resource type and date range
body:
## Problem

`QueryStoreService.search(query, limit)` takes only a query string and a result cap. Consumers cannot scope a cross-patient search to a specific resource type (e.g. 'obs only', 'conditions only') or to a date range, even though the backend `SearchRequest` builder supports both filters internally.

## Use case (chartsearchai)

`RetrievalQuery` in chartsearchai post-filters by resource type on the client side, which is fine when working from a `listByPatient` bulk fetch. But for any future use case that wants cross-patient cohort-style search ('all patients with a condition matching X in the last 30 days'), the filtering would have to be re-done in the consumer — wasted bandwidth and a worse top-K selection because the limit is applied before filtering.

## Proposed API

Surface the existing internal filters:

```java
List<QueryDocument> search(SearchRequest request);

class SearchRequest {
    String query;
    int limit;
    List<String> resourceTypes;     // optional
    Instant from;                    // optional
    Instant to;                      // optional
    String patientUuid;              // optional (already covered by searchByPatient)
}
```

Keep the existing `search(query, limit)` and `searchByPatient(uuid, query, limit)` as thin wrappers for backward compat.

## Size

Small. Plumbing only — the backends already accept these filters; the service interface just needs to pass them through.

## Priority

Nice-to-have for chartsearchai migration (not blocking — chartsearchai filters client-side today). Worth doing early since the API shape will be harder to change once consumers calcify around `search(query, limit)`.

title: Expose ensureIndexed via REST for warmup on patient chart load
body:
## Problem

Cold-patient queries pay a real latency cost: even with auto-index-on-empty (#7), the first query against an unindexed patient blocks on serialization + embedding of that patient's entire chart before any results come back. A clinician asking a question and waiting 10–30 seconds for the first response is a measurably worse experience than 1–2 seconds for subsequent queries.

The fix is warmup: trigger indexing as soon as the clinician opens the patient's chart, so that by the time they actually type a question, the patient is already (or nearly) indexed and the search returns at steady-state latency.

Issue #5 proposes `ensureIndexed(patientUuid)` as a Java service method, which gives backend consumers what they need. But the natural trigger for warmup — 'clinician just opened a patient chart' — fires in the frontend (OpenMRS RefApp 3 / O3 ESM, chartsearchai SPA, third-party charts), not in a server-side advice point. Without a REST endpoint, frontends have to either route through a consumer module's controller or skip warmup entirely.

querystore currently has no REST controllers (`omod/src/main/resources/config.xml` is the only omod resource; no `webservices.rest` integration), so this is net-new surface.

## Proposed API

Add a webservices.rest resource:

```
POST /ws/rest/v1/querystore/ensureindexed/{patientUuid}
```

Body: empty. Returns `202 Accepted` immediately with a small JSON envelope:

```json
{
  "patientUuid": "...",
  "status": "ALREADY_INDEXED" | "INDEXING_STARTED",
  "documentCount": 142
}
```

Behavior:
- If the patient already has documents indexed: no-op, return `ALREADY_INDEXED` with current count.
- If not: invoke the same per-patient indexing primitive backing #5 and #7, run on a background executor, return immediately with `INDEXING_STARTED`.

This is fire-and-forget warmup by design — the endpoint never blocks on the projection. Callers that need to coordinate with completion should rely on the auto-index-on-empty path in `searchByPatient` (#7) instead.

[word removed]: same `@Authorized(PrivilegeConstants.GET_PATIENTS)` as `searchByPatient`.

## Consumer integration

Frontend wires the call into the patient-chart-load hook:

```js
fetch(`/openmrs/ws/rest/v1/querystore/ensureindexed/${patientUuid}`, { method: 'POST' });
// No await — fire and forget
```

Cost: one HTTP request per chart open, returning immediately. Indexing runs in the background. By the time the clinician composes a question and submits it, the index is warm.

## Relationship to other issues

- **#5** — service-level `ensureIndexed` is the prerequisite. This issue is the REST veneer on top.
- **#7** — auto-index-on-empty inside `searchByPatient` is the safety net for cases where warmup wasn't triggered or hasn't finished. This issue is the optimistic path: warm up early so the safety net rarely fires.
- All three should share one per-patient indexing primitive on `BootstrapService`.

## Size

Small to medium. New webservices.rest resource class, background executor + bounded queue, integration test against a real MySQL backend, and a brief usage section in the README.

## Open design questions

- The background path should be bounded. On a deployment where dozens of clinicians open dozens of charts simultaneously, queueing every patient for projection could starve the executor. A bounded queue with bounded concurrency (e.g. 4 in-flight indexings) and 'already-queued' deduplication is probably right.
- Should the endpoint return `documentCount` honestly, or omit it to avoid leaking chart size? `GET_PATIENTS` [word removed] already implies the caller can see the chart, so the count is not sensitive.

title: Auto-index patient on first search when no documents exist
body:
## Problem

`QueryStoreService.searchByPatient(patientUuid, query, limit)` returns an empty list when the patient has no indexed documents (see `QueryStoreServiceImpl.java:73-79` → `runHybrid` against an empty backend). There is no fallback path that triggers indexing for that patient.

In deployments without scheduled backfill — for example chartsearchai's demo server at `chartsearchai.openmrs.org`, which has limited resources and no batch job — a first-touch query against a patient who has never been indexed silently returns nothing. The user perceives this as 'querystore doesn't know about my patient' rather than 'querystore hasn't gotten around to indexing them yet'.

## Proposed behaviour

Inside `searchByPatient`, if the backend reports zero documents for the given `patientUuid`:

1. Synchronously project that patient's clinical data into the store using the configured serializers and embedding provider — i.e. run the same per-patient indexing path that `BootstrapService` runs per resource type, but scoped to one patient.
2. Re-run the search.
3. Return the result.

Idempotent: if any document exists for the patient (even one), the auto-index step is skipped and the search runs normally. This keeps the steady-state cost zero and only pays the projection cost on cold patients.

Thread-safety: concurrent first-touch on the same patient must not double-index. A per-patient lock or a 'started-at' marker in the bootstrap progress table is enough — version-protected last-write-wins on the document upserts already handles the rest.

This should be the unconditional default behavior — no opt-out toggle. Returning empty results for an unindexed patient is silently wrong, and any consumer who wants predictable search latency can pre-bootstrap or schedule periodic backfills instead of opting into a footgun.

## Relationship to #5

Issue #5 proposes an explicit `ensureIndexed(patientUuid)` method consumers call before searching. This issue proposes that `searchByPatient` does the right thing on its own. The two are complementary: `ensureIndexed` is useful for warmup flows where the consumer knows it's about to query a cold patient (e.g. on patient chart load), and the auto-index inside `searchByPatient` is the safety net for everyone else. Both should be backed by the same internal per-patient indexing primitive.

## Use case (chartsearchai)

chartsearchai's `LuceneIndexer.hasIndex(patient)` probe (`HybridRetriever.java:62-73`) does exactly this for the Lucene pipeline today: check existence, index lazily if absent, then search. Migrating off that probe onto querystore is fine *if* querystore handles the lazy path itself — otherwise every consumer reinvents the same wheel.

## Size

Medium. Implementation reuses `BootstrapService`'s per-resource-type projection logic scoped down to one patient. Needs:
- A `BackendStore.countByPatient(uuid)` (or a cheap `existsByPatient`) — small SPI addition
- A per-patient indexing path on `BootstrapService` (overlaps with issue #5)
- Concurrency control for racing first-touch queries on the same patient
- Tests covering: cold patient → search → docs indexed → results returned; concurrent first-touch; index-failure fallback

## Related

- #5 — `ensureIndexed` as an explicit primitive (complementary; shares the same internal indexing path)
- #2 — Whole-patient document listing (uses the same 'has any docs for this patient' check)

title: Module startup fails: NoSuchBeanDefinitionException for 'dataSource' in MysqlBackendStore
body:
## Problem

The querystore module fails to start on OpenMRS 2.8.5 (standalone Reference Application 3.6.0). Spring refuses to instantiate `querystore.backend.mysql` because the `dataSource` bean it expects via constructor-arg is not exposed in the OpenMRS module Spring context.

Without this, querystore can't be installed alongside chartsearchai, which blocks end-to-end testing of [chartsearchai's querystore migration flag](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/commit/0215d81).

## Reproduction

1. Fresh OpenMRS Platform 2.8.5 standalone (Reference Application 3.6.0).
2. `mvn clean install` querystore at HEAD of `main` → drop `querystore-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.omod` into `appdata/modules/`.
3. Start OpenMRS.
4. Module load fails; OpenMRS returns HTTP 500 on all subsequent REST calls.

## Stack trace

```
WARN AbstractApplicationContext.refresh - Exception encountered during context initialization:
org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanCreationException: Error creating bean with name
'querystore.backend.mysql' defined in URL [...moduleApplicationContext.xml]:
Cannot resolve reference to bean 'dataSource' while setting constructor argument;
nested exception is org.springframework.beans.factory.NoSuchBeanDefinitionException:
No bean named 'dataSource' available
    at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.BeanDefinitionValueResolver
       .resolveReference(BeanDefinitionValueResolver.java:342)
    ...
    at org.openmrs.module.ModuleUtil.refreshApplicationContext(ModuleUtil.java:891)
    at org.openmrs.module.web.WebModuleUtil.refreshWAC(WebModuleUtil.java:948)
    at org.openmrs.web.Listener.performWebStartOfModules(Listener.java:722)
    at org.openmrs.web.Listener.startOpenmrs(Listener.java:361)

ERROR Listener.contextInitialized - Failed to obtain JDBC connection
org.openmrs.module.ModuleException: Unable to start OpenMRS. Error thrown was: [same as above]
```

## Root cause

`api/src/main/resources/moduleApplicationContext.xml` wires the MySQL backend with:

```xml
<bean id="querystore.backend.mysql"
      class="org.openmrs.module.querystore.backend.mysql.MysqlBackendStore">
    <constructor-arg ref="dataSource"/>
</bean>
```

OpenMRS 2.x doesn't expose a top-level Spring bean named `dataSource` to modules at module-load time. OpenMRS modules consume the database via either:

- **`SessionFactory`** (`org.openmrs.api.db.hibernate.HibernateUtil.getSessionFactory()` or autowire `org.hibernate.SessionFactory`), or
- **`HibernateDaoSupport`** extension on the DAO class

The same `<constructor-arg ref="dataSource"/>` pattern appears at `moduleApplicationContext.xml:92` for what looks like the bootstrap DAO — the same fix likely applies there.

## Suggested fix

Replace the raw `dataSource` injection with the OpenMRS-standard `SessionFactory` injection. The `MysqlBackendStore` (and the bootstrap DAO at line 92) should accept `SessionFactory` and obtain a `Connection` via `sessionFactory.getCurrentSession().doWork(...)` when raw JDBC is needed.

Alternative: derive `DataSource` from `SessionFactory.getProperties()` once at startup if the backend genuinely needs a `DataSource` reference rather than per-call connection access. But the simpler shape is to operate through Hibernate sessions like the rest of OpenMRS.

For reference, `openmrs-module-chartsearchai` ships with only `<context:component-scan>` in its `moduleApplicationContext.xml` — DAOs autowire `SessionFactory` directly. No `dataSource` bean reference anywhere.

## Environment

- OpenMRS Platform: 2.8.5
- Reference Application: 3.6.0 (standalone)
- Database: MariaDB (bundled with standalone)
- Java: OpenJDK 21
- querystore commit: HEAD of `main` (1.0.0-SNAPSHOT) as of 2026-05-15

title: Module startup deadlocks: BackendStoreSelector.resolveBackendName() calls Context.getAdministrationService() during Spring init
body:
## Problem

After [#9](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-querystore/issues/9) was fixed (`dbSessionFactory` injection), querystore now reaches bean construction — but module startup still deadlocks before HTTP comes up. No error is logged; OpenMRS sits silent past `INFO ServiceContext.startRefreshingContext - Refreshing Context` indefinitely.

This blocks chartsearchai's end-to-end test of the querystore migration flag — and would block any consumer running querystore on the OpenMRS standalone / RefApp 3 deployment shape.

## Root cause

`BackendStoreSelector.getStore()` is wired as a Spring `factory-method`, so it runs during context refresh. It calls `resolveBackendName()`, which calls `Context.getAdministrationService()`. In OpenMRS 2.x, `ServiceContext.getService()` blocks on `wait()` while `refreshingContext == true` — and refresh can't complete until every bean (including this one) finishes constructing. Classic Spring-during-init deadlock.

The comment at `BackendStoreSelector.java:68-70` is the bug:

```java
// AdministrationService is registered with the core context before any module context
// loads, so this call is safe at module bean init — but defend against test contexts
// that bypass the framework by treating any lookup failure as "use the default".
try {
    AdministrationService admin = Context.getAdministrationService();
    ...
}
catch (RuntimeException e) {
    log.warn("Could not read " + QueryStoreConstants.GP_BACKEND + " GP; using default", e);
}
```

Registration ≠ availability. `Context.getAdministrationService()` blocks indefinitely while the same refresh is in progress, and the catch is for `RuntimeException` — `Object.wait()` doesn't throw, so the fallback never fires.

## Thread dump

Diagnostic thread dump while hung (OpenMRS 2.8.5 standalone, RefApp 3.6.0):

```
\"pool-24-thread-1\" #84 in Object.wait()
    at java.lang.Object.wait(java.base@21.0.6/Object.java:339)
    at org.openmrs.api.context.ServiceContext.getService(ServiceContext.java:683)
    - locked <0x00000007e21dda60> (a java.lang.Object)
    at org.openmrs.api.context.ServiceContext.getAdministrationService(ServiceContext.java:306)
    at org.openmrs.api.context.Context.getAdministrationService(Context.java:528)
    at org.openmrs.module.querystore.backend.BackendStoreSelector.resolveBackendName(BackendStoreSelector.java:72)
    at org.openmrs.module.querystore.backend.BackendStoreSelector.getStore(BackendStoreSelector.java:51)
    at [Spring factory-method instantiation]
```

The same thread is **holding** monitor `0x00000007e21dda60` (Spring's wait on ServiceContext) and also **waiting** on it — self-deadlock. Other `pool-24-thread-N` (the OpenMRS service-startup pool) queue behind the same monitor; all module startups stall.

Effect from outside: HTTP never comes up, no error in `tomcat/logs/*.log` past `Refreshing Context`, IdgenTask warning every 5 minutes confirms the JVM is alive but `WebDaemon.startOpenmrs` is parked.

## Reproduction

1. OpenMRS Platform 2.8.5, RefApp 3.6.0 standalone, MariaDB (bundled).
2. Drop `querystore-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.omod` (at HEAD of `main` with #9 fix applied) into `appdata/modules/`.
3. Start OpenMRS.
4. Wait. HTTP never serves; thread dump shows the stack above.

## Suggested fix

Don't read GPs during bean construction. Options:

- **Resolve lazily.** Make `BackendStore` a wrapper that defers `getStore()` to first call by consumers (after module activation). Consumers already get a `BackendStore` reference via Spring; the wrapper proxies through to the chosen tier on first non-init invocation.
- **Use `ModuleActivator.started()`.** `QueryStoreActivator.started()` already runs after context refresh completes. Resolve the active backend there and inject it into `QueryStoreServiceImpl` (or expose it via `BackendStoreSelector.getStore()` then). At Spring wiring time, `BackendStoreSelector` should hold only the candidate map.
- **Spring `SmartLifecycle` / `@PostConstruct` on a wrapper bean.** Same shape as the activator option, kept Spring-native.

The simplest is option 2: remove `factory-method="getStore"` from the `moduleApplicationContext.xml` definition of `querystore.backend`, wire `BackendStoreSelector` as a plain bean, and resolve the backend in `QueryStoreActivator.started()` (which already runs after refresh completes).

Side note: the catch block at `BackendStoreSelector.java:81-83` catches `RuntimeException`, but `Object.wait()` doesn't throw — the "defensive fallback" comment is a no-op in practice. Worth removing the catch when the lookup moves to a safe location.

## Environment

- OpenMRS Platform: 2.8.5
- Reference Application: 3.6.0 (standalone)
- Database: MariaDB (bundled)
- Java: OpenJDK 21
- querystore commit: HEAD of `main` (1.0.0-SNAPSHOT) after #9 fix, as of 2026-05-15
- chartsearchai commit: `0215d81` (with querystore migration flag, currently off)

title: MysqlSchemaManager.listAllTables() includes querystore_bootstrap_progress; bm25/knn fail with 'Unknown column resource_uuid'
body:
## Problem

After [#9](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-querystore/issues/9) and [#10](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-querystore/issues/10) shipped, `QueryStoreService.searchByPatient(uuid, query, limit)` is reachable end-to-end — but it fails on the MySQL backend whenever there are zero per-type indices yet. `bm25` enumerates `querystore_bootstrap_progress` as if it were a document table, then issues a `SELECT resource_uuid, ...` against it. The bootstrap-progress table has no `resource_uuid` column, so the query throws `SQLSyntaxErrorException`.

Net effect: every search on a fresh install (or any deployment where the per-type tables haven't been materialised yet) crashes. The chartsearchai migration flag falls through to its catch and degrades to "no relevant records," masking the root cause from the user.

## Root cause

`MysqlSchemaManager.listAllTables()` at `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/querystore/backend/mysql/MysqlSchemaManager.java:96` uses a JDBC metadata probe with the LIKE pattern `querystore_%`:

```java
try (ResultSet rs = md.getTables(conn.getCatalog(), null, QueryStoreConstants.INDEX_PREFIX + "%",
    new String[] { "TABLE" })) {
    while (rs.next()) {
        tables.add(rs.getString("TABLE_NAME").toLowerCase());
    }
}
```

`INDEX_PREFIX` is `"querystore_"` (`QueryStoreConstants.java:16`). The pattern matches both:
- Per-type indices: `querystore_obs`, `querystore_condition`, etc. (each has `resource_uuid`, `text`, `embedding`, etc. — defined by `ensureTable(resourceType)`).
- Bootstrap state: `querystore_bootstrap_progress` (PK `resource_type`, columns `status`, `cursor_*`, `documents_indexed`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `failure_message` — no `resource_uuid`).

`MysqlBackendStore.bm25` (line 267) and `knn` (line 281) call `resolveTables(req)` (line 434) which, for a wildcard query, returns whatever `listAllTables()` produces. They then call `bm25SingleTable(table, req)` per result, which prepares a SQL statement assuming the per-type-index schema:

```
SELECT resource_uuid, ... FROM querystore_bootstrap_progress WHERE ...
   → SQLSyntaxErrorException: Unknown column 'resource_uuid'
```

## Reproduction

1. OpenMRS Platform 2.8.5 standalone (RefApp 3.6.0), MariaDB bundled.
2. Install both `chartsearchai` (with the querystore migration flag enabled) and `querystore` omods.
3. Set `chartsearchai.querystore.enabled = true`, configure `querystore.embedding.modelFilePath` and `vocabFilePath`.
4. Start OpenMRS — both modules report `STARTED`. `Query Store backend resolved: mysql` appears in the log.
5. `SHOW TABLES FROM openmrs LIKE 'querystore_%'` shows only `querystore_bootstrap_progress` — no per-type indices yet (no patients have been indexed; `querystore.bootstrap.autostart=false`).
6. Issue a chartsearchai search:
   ```
   POST /openmrs/ws/rest/v1/chartsearchai/search
   { "patient": "<uuid>", "question": "any vital signs?" }
   ```
7. Response: `{"answer":"No relevant records found.","references":[]}`. Log shows the stack below.

## Stack trace

```
ERROR SqlExceptionHelper.logExceptions - (conn=42) Unknown column 'resource_uuid' in 'SELECT'
ERROR QueryStoreChartBuilder.build - QueryStore search failed for patient [uuid=07e26b8e-00a9-4b31-b805-3560ad4e9e2e]
java.lang.IllegalStateException: BM25 query on querystore_bootstrap_progress failed
    at org.openmrs.module.querystore.backend.mysql.MysqlBackendStore.bm25SingleTable(MysqlBackendStore.java:390)
    at org.openmrs.module.querystore.backend.mysql.MysqlBackendStore.bm25(MysqlBackendStore.java:273)
    at org.openmrs.module.querystore.api.impl.QueryStoreServiceImpl.runHybrid(QueryStoreServiceImpl.java:135)
    at org.openmrs.module.querystore.api.impl.QueryStoreServiceImpl.searchByPatient(QueryStoreServiceImpl.java:93)
    at jdk.proxy8/jdk.proxy8.$Proxy334.searchByPatient(Unknown Source)
    at org.openmrs.module.chartsearchai.api.impl.QueryStoreChartBuilder.build(QueryStoreChartBuilder.java:64)
    ...
Caused by: java.sql.SQLSyntaxErrorException: (conn=42) Unknown column 'resource_uuid' in 'SELECT'
    at org.mariadb.jdbc.export.ExceptionFactory.createException(ExceptionFactory.java:289)
    ...
    at org.openmrs.module.querystore.backend.mysql.MysqlBackendStore.lambda$bm25SingleTable$8(MysqlBackendStore.java:379)
```

## Suggested fixes

Any one of the following — or a defence-in-depth combination — addresses the immediate bug:

- **Filter the metadata probe.** In `MysqlSchemaManager.listAllTables()`, exclude `bootstrap_progress` (and any future state-only tables) explicitly. A constant set of known state tables works; or rename the bootstrap table to `querystore_state_bootstrap_progress` and filter by a different prefix.
- **Use a more specific naming convention for per-type indices.** E.g., `querystore_idx_<type>` for indices and `querystore_state_<name>` for state tables. The README and ADR Decision 4 already discuss the `openmrs_<type>` shape (and `openmrs_<moduleid>_<type>` for module-contributed types) — picking one and migrating end-to-end resolves this without ad-hoc filtering.
- **Guard `bm25SingleTable` / `knnSingleTable`.** Check the table has a `resource_uuid` column (via `DatabaseMetaData.getColumns`) before issuing the search SQL, and skip with a debug log if not. Robust but masks future drift.

The wildcard-search case (zero per-type tables exist yet) is also worth thinking about: today it returns `IllegalStateException` from the very first failing table; consumers can't tell "no indexed data" from "backend bug" at the call site. After the filter, the natural outcome is `SearchResult.empty()`, which `searchByPatient` already handles as zero hits.

## Related: `existsByPatient` behavior

Separate concern, but surfaces in the same trace: `searchByPatient` calls `backend.existsByPatient(patientUuid)` first to decide whether to lazy-bootstrap (issue [#7](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-querystore/issues/7)). If `existsByPatient` returns true (e.g., the patient's row in `querystore_bootstrap_progress` exists from a prior incomplete run), the lazy-bootstrap is skipped — and then `runHybrid` immediately fails on the same table-list problem above. Worth checking whether `existsByPatient` also has the same wildcard issue.

## Environment

- OpenMRS Platform: 2.8.5
- Reference Application: 3.6.0 (standalone)
- Database: MariaDB (bundled)
- Java: OpenJDK 21
- querystore commit: HEAD of `main` (1.0.0-SNAPSHOT) after #9 and #10 fixes, as of 2026-05-15
- chartsearchai commit: `0215d81` plus a local `aware_of_modules` patch on `omod/src/main/resources/config.xml` (so chartsearchai's classloader can see querystore — needed to surface this bug at all)

title: BootstrapService not registered with ServiceContext; ensureIndexedSafely fails on every cold-patient search
body:
## Problem

After fixes for #9, #10, and #11 landed, `QueryStoreService.searchByPatient` is reachable and the MySQL backend's table-enumeration bug is gone. But every cold-patient search still returns zero results — the lazy bootstrap path inside `QueryStoreServiceImpl.ensureIndexedSafely` throws because `Context.getService(BootstrapService.class)` can't find the service:

```
WARN  QueryStoreServiceImpl.ensureIndexedSafely - Auto-index for patient 07e26b8e-... failed;
       serving search with whatever is indexed
org.openmrs.api.ServiceNotFoundException: Service not found:
       interface org.openmrs.module.querystore.bootstrap.BootstrapService
```

Net effect: `searchByPatient(patientUuid, q, limit)` for any never-indexed patient silently returns `[]` and consumers (chartsearchai's migration flag, future REST callers from #8) get a wrong-but-not-erroring "no records" outcome. The catch is by design (per the javadoc — index failure shouldn't block search), so the failure is invisible at the API boundary.

## Reproduction

1. OpenMRS Platform 2.8.5 standalone (RefApp 3.6.0), MariaDB bundled.
2. Install querystore HEAD of `main` (post-#9, #10, #11) and chartsearchai with the querystore migration flag enabled.
3. Set `querystore.embedding.modelFilePath` / `vocabFilePath` (e.g. all-MiniLM-L6-v2), `chartsearchai.querystore.enabled = true`. Leave `querystore.bootstrap.autostart = false`.
4. Start OpenMRS — both modules report `STARTED`. `Query Store backend resolved: mysql` appears in the log.
5. Verify `BootstrapService` is reachable as a Spring bean (you can confirm via the activator's wiring of `queryStoreService` — `queryStoreService` IS findable via `Context.getService`, see step 6).
6. Issue a chartsearchai search:
   ```
   POST /openmrs/ws/rest/v1/chartsearchai/search
   { "patient": "<uuid>", "question": "any vital signs?" }
   ```
7. Response: `{"answer":"No relevant records found.","references":[]}`. Log shows the `ServiceNotFoundException` above. `SHOW TABLES FROM openmrs LIKE 'querystore_%'` shows only `querystore_bootstrap_progress` — per-type tables never created, so the lazy bootstrap never ran.

## Root cause

`api/src/main/resources/moduleApplicationContext.xml` registers both services in a single `<bean parent="serviceContext">` with a 4-element list:

```xml
<bean parent="serviceContext">
    <property name="moduleService">
        <list>
            <value>org.openmrs.module.querystore.api.QueryStoreService</value>
            <ref bean="queryStoreService"/>
            <value>org.openmrs.module.querystore.bootstrap.BootstrapService</value>
            <ref bean="bootstrapService"/>
        </list>
    </property>
</bean>
```

OpenMRS's `ServiceContext.setModuleService(List)` expects a 2-element list — `[interfaceClassName, beanInstance]` — and the property setter is invoked once per `<bean parent="serviceContext">`. Passing four elements means only the first pair gets registered; `QueryStoreService` lands in the service map, `BootstrapService` is silently dropped.

Evidence from the same demo:
- `Context.getService(QueryStoreService.class)` returns the AOP proxy successfully (chartsearchai's migration flag reaches `searchByPatient`).
- `Context.getService(BootstrapService.class)` throws `ServiceNotFoundException` immediately.

## Suggested fix

Split into two `<bean parent="serviceContext">` beans — the conventional OpenMRS shape:

```xml
<bean parent="serviceContext">
    <property name="moduleService">
        <list>
            <value>org.openmrs.module.querystore.api.QueryStoreService</value>
            <ref bean="queryStoreService"/>
        </list>
    </property>
</bean>

<bean parent="serviceContext">
    <property name="moduleService">
        <list>
            <value>org.openmrs.module.querystore.bootstrap.BootstrapService</value>
            <ref bean="bootstrapService"/>
        </list>
    </property>
</bean>
```

One service registration per parent bean. Mirrors how every other OpenMRS module that ships multiple services does it.

## Side note: `existsByPatient` returns false but bootstrap is skipped

Worth a quick verification: even after `BootstrapService` becomes reachable, `ensureIndexedSafely` is invoked only when `backend.existsByPatient(patientUuid)` returns false. On the demo, `querystore_bootstrap_progress` exists from earlier runs and may contain the patient's `resource_type` rows from a partial prior bootstrap — would `existsByPatient` mistakenly return true based on bootstrap-progress state rather than actual per-type documents? Probably fine (existsByPatient should query per-type indices for `patient_uuid`, not `bootstrap_progress`), but worth a defensive integration test once #11 and this one ship together.

## Environment

- OpenMRS Platform: 2.8.5
- Reference Application: 3.6.0 (standalone)
- Database: MariaDB (bundled)
- Java: OpenJDK 21
- querystore commit: HEAD of `main` (1.0.0-SNAPSHOT) after #9, #10, and #11 fixes, as of 2026-05-15
- chartsearchai commit: `c091f98` (`aware_of_modules` declaration for querystore + querystore migration flag)

title: Lucene backend fails on OpenMRS standalone: Lucene87Codec from core's Hibernate Search collides with querystore's Lucene 9.x SPI
body:
## Problem

Setting `querystore.backend=lucene` on OpenMRS 2.8.5 standalone (RefApp 3.6.0) makes every search throw a `ServiceConfigurationError` at first use. The Lucene tier appears unusable in any OpenMRS standalone deployment.

```
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class org.apache.lucene.codecs.Codec$Holder
Caused by: java.util.ServiceConfigurationError: org.apache.lucene.codecs.Codec:
  org.apache.lucene.codecs.lucene87.Lucene87Codec not a subtype
```

The MySQL tier on the same standalone works end-to-end (verified — all of #9/#10/#11/#12 land cleanly with `backend=mysql`, including lazy bootstrap, per-type index creation, and `searchByPatient` returning real top-K hits). Only the Lucene tier breaks.

## Root cause

Two Lucene versions are visible to the same ServiceLoader call:

- **OpenMRS core** ships Hibernate Search 5.x, which depends on **Lucene 8.x** (8.11.x in the 2.8.5 standalone). Lucene 8 includes `org.apache.lucene.codecs.lucene87.Lucene87Codec` and registers it in `META-INF/services/org.apache.lucene.codecs.Codec`.
- **Querystore omod** bundles **Lucene 9.11.1** (`lucene-core-9.11.1.jar` and friends in `omod/.../lib/`). Lucene 9 dropped `Lucene87Codec` entirely.

When `LuceneBackendStore` initializes, the SPI `ServiceLoader<Codec>` traverses every `META-INF/services/org.apache.lucene.codecs.Codec` on the classpath. It finds the `Lucene87Codec` entry from core's Lucene 8 jars and tries to instantiate it as a subtype of the Lucene 9 `Codec` class querystore loaded — not a subtype error.

## Reproduction

1. OpenMRS Platform 2.8.5 standalone (RefApp 3.6.0), MariaDB bundled. Lucene 8.x present transitively via Hibernate Search.
2. Install querystore HEAD of `main` (post-#9/#10/#11/#12) and chartsearchai with the querystore migration flag enabled.
3. Set `querystore.backend = lucene`, `querystore.embedding.modelFilePath`/`vocabFilePath`, `chartsearchai.querystore.enabled = true`. Restart.
4. Confirm activator log: `Query Store backend resolved: lucene`. Startup completes cleanly.
5. Issue a chartsearchai search:
   ```
   POST /openmrs/ws/rest/v1/chartsearchai/search
   { "patient": "<uuid>", "question": "any vital signs?" }
   ```
6. Response is an HTTP 500 with the chain above; no `querystore_*` Lucene index directory ever gets created under `<appdata>/querystore/lucene/`.

## Suggested fixes

Pick one:

1. **Shade the Lucene dependency.** Use the `maven-shade-plugin` in querystore's omod build to relocate `org.apache.lucene.*` → e.g. `org.openmrs.module.querystore.shaded.lucene.*`. Removes the SPI collision entirely since the shaded classes register under different `META-INF/services` paths. Standard pattern when a module bundles a library that core also uses transitively.
2. **Downgrade to a Lucene version compatible with OpenMRS core's Hibernate Search.** Use the same 8.x line core uses. Costs: lose Lucene 9 features (HNSW kNN improvements, etc.). Lucene 9 HNSW is what made the "medium" tier viable per ADR Decision 3, so this is a real regression.
3. **Explicit codec selection bypassing SPI.** Pass an explicit `Codec` instance to `IndexWriterConfig.setCodec(...)` and `IndexReader` consumers, so ServiceLoader never has to resolve a default. Closes the immediate bug but doesn't prevent future SPI clashes (e.g. `PostingsFormat`, `DocValuesFormat` — same shape).

(1) is the only durable solution; (3) is the cheapest workaround if shading is too invasive for v1.

## Impact

The Lucene tier is the "medium" tier per [ADR Decision 3](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-querystore/blob/main/docs/adr.md#decision-3-pluggable-backend-spi-with-three-reference-implementations) — meant to be the no-new-infrastructure default for sites that have outgrown MySQL kNN but don't want an Elasticsearch cluster. In an OpenMRS standalone deployment (which is the typical RefApp shape), it's currently a dead path: MySQL tier or external Elasticsearch are the only working options.

## Environment

- Reference Application: 3.6.0 (standalone)

title: ElasticsearchBackendStore.upsert/bulkUpsert skip ensureIndex; ES auto-mapping makes patient_uuid 'text', patient-scope filter returns 0 hits
body:
## Problem

On the Elasticsearch tier, every `searchByPatient(uuid, query, limit)` call returns zero hits even when the indices are populated. The cold-bootstrap step writes ~671 documents to ES successfully (visible via `_cat/indices`, all docs present), but no subsequent search finds them — because the patient-scope filter never matches.

Real consequence: chartsearchai's querystore migration flag, with `querystore.backend=elasticsearch`, returns an empty chart for every patient. The LLM answers "No relevant records found" regardless of what's indexed.

## Root cause

`ElasticsearchBackendStore.upsert(QueryDocument)` (`ElasticsearchBackendStore.java:108`) calls `client.index(...)` directly without calling `schemaManager.ensureIndex(...)` first. `bulkUpsert` (`ElasticsearchBackendStore.java:166`) and its `executeBulkUpsert` helper have the same gap.

When ES receives the first index request for a non-existent index, it auto-creates that index with **default dynamic mapping** — which maps string fields as `text` plus a `.keyword` sub-field, **not** as plain `keyword`. So the live mapping is:

```
patient_uuid: type=text, fields=[keyword]
resource_uuid: type=text, fields=[keyword]
```

But the SPI filter translator generates `term` queries against the **bare** field name (`ElasticsearchFilterTranslator.java`):

```java
case TERM:
case PATIENT_SCOPE:
    return termQuery(f.getField(), f.getValue());
```

A `term` query on a `text` field doesn't match the UUID literally — `text` fields are analyzed and tokenized, so the UUID gets broken into pieces and the exact-term match silently fails. Reproducible directly against ES:

```
$ curl -s 'localhost:9200/querystore_obs/_search?size=0' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"query":{"term":{"patient_uuid":"07e26b8e-00a9-4b31-b805-3560ad4e9e2e"}}}'
{"hits":{"total":{"value":0,"relation":"eq"}}}

$ curl -s 'localhost:9200/querystore_obs/_search?size=0' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"query":{"term":{"patient_uuid.keyword":"07e26b8e-00a9-4b31-b805-3560ad4e9e2e"}}}'
{"hits":{"total":{"value":400,"relation":"eq"}}}
```

`ElasticsearchSchemaManager.buildMapping(...)` (line 149-150) does declare these fields as `keyword`:

```java
properties.put(ElasticsearchFieldNames.RESOURCE_UUID, Property.of(p -> p.keyword(k -> k)));
properties.put(ElasticsearchFieldNames.PATIENT_UUID, Property.of(p -> p.keyword(k -> k)));
```

…but `createIndex` is never invoked because `upsert/bulkUpsert` skip the `ensureIndex` call. The explicit mapping never gets applied.

For comparison: `MysqlBackendStore.batchUpsert` (`MysqlBackendStore.java:328`) calls `schemaManager.ensureTable(resourceType)` before each batch. That's why the MySQL tier works end-to-end on the same demo.

The contract is documented in `ResourceTypeProvider.java:40` ("Lucene and Elasticsearch backends call `ensureSchema` lazily on the first upsert per resource type") — just not implemented on the ES backend.

## Reproduction

1. OpenMRS Platform 2.8.5 standalone (RefApp 3.6.0), MariaDB bundled.
2. ES 8.13.4 running locally (`docker run -d -p 9200:9200 -e "discovery.type=single-node" -e "xpack.security.enabled=false" docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.13.4`).
3. Install querystore HEAD of `main` (post-#9/#10/#11/#12/#13) and chartsearchai with the querystore migration flag enabled.
4. Set `querystore.elasticsearch.uri=http://localhost:9200` in `openmrs-runtime.properties`, `querystore.backend=elasticsearch`, `chartsearchai.querystore.enabled=true`.
5. Restart. Activator log: `Query Store backend resolved: elasticsearch`.
6. Issue a chartsearchai search. Cold bootstrap takes ~12 minutes (see secondary issue below); when it completes, response is `{"answer":"No relevant records found.","references":[]}`.
7. Verify ES has docs: `curl localhost:9200/_cat/indices?v` shows `querystore_obs` with 400 docs (and others). Patient UUID is present in `_source` — but `term` queries don't match the bare field.

## Suggested fix

Two options, both minor:

1. **Call `ensureSchema` before the first write per resource type.** Mirror `MysqlBackendStore.batchUpsert` — at the top of `upsert(QueryDocument)` and `executeBulkUpsert(...)`, call `schemaManager.ensureIndex(doc.getResourceType(), doc.getEmbeddingDimensions())`. The `ElasticsearchSchemaManager.ensureIndex` is already idempotent and dim-cached, so the overhead is just a `Map.get` after the first call.
2. **Translate `patient_uuid` and `resource_uuid` term filters to use the `.keyword` sub-field** in `ElasticsearchFilterTranslator`. Cheaper but encodes a dynamic-mapping detail into the translator and only fixes existing broken indices — new indices keep the wrong shape, and any future `text`-mapped field gets a similar gotcha.

(1) is the durable fix. The mapping declared in `buildMapping(...)` is the right shape; just make sure it's applied.

## Secondary: cold-bootstrap latency

Separate concern (and an existing [ADR open question](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-querystore/blob/main/docs/adr.md#backend-spi-contract--residual)), but it surfaces in the same trace: the cold-bootstrap call took **12 minutes 6 seconds** to return for a single patient with 671 documents on this demo. `refresh=wait_for` per doc × 1s default `refresh_interval` × 671 ≈ 12 min. Matches the ADR's note that "the eval measured a 142s indexing cost for a 153-record benchmark at default `refresh_interval=1s` — fine for steady-state event sync, painful for bootstrap fan-out."

That open question stays as-is; this issue is only about the schema bug.

## Environment

- OpenMRS Platform: 2.8.5
- Reference Application: 3.6.0 (standalone)
- Elasticsearch: 8.13.4 (Docker, single-node, security disabled)
- Java: OpenJDK 21
- querystore commit: HEAD of `main` (1.0.0-SNAPSHOT) after #9/#10/#11/#12/#13 fixes, as of 2026-05-15
- chartsearchai commit: `0ca730e` (querystore migration flag + `aware_of_modules` + declared GPs)

title: Validate AbstractIndexingAdvice TRIGGER_METHODS at bean init against the target service interface
body:
## Problem

\`AbstractIndexingAdvice\` matches advised invocations by method **name** against the configured \`triggerMethods()\` and \`purgeMethods()\` sets. A typo, rename, or stale name produces:

- No compile error
- No startup error
- No runtime exception
- No log

The advice simply never fires. The failure surfaces only as \"stale rows in the read store\" some time later — often days or weeks after the typo was introduced.

This is a class of silent-failure bug that every consumer module has to defend against. In billing we mitigated with a reflection-based \`IndexingAdviceConfigTest\` that asserts every name in \`TRIGGER_METHODS\` and \`PURGE_METHODS\` resolves to a method on the target service interface, and that purge is a subset of trigger (per the SPI contract). See the billing PR for the test shape: https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-billing/pull/176

The problem is that every consumer module has to reinvent this test. The querystore SPI knows the trigger/purge sets and could validate them in one place.

## Suggested approach

\`AbstractIndexingAdvice\` already knows \`getSupportedType()\` and the trigger/purge sets. It does NOT currently know the *service interface* the advice is registered against (that's declared in \`omod/config.xml\`'s \`<advice><point>\` element, not on the advice class itself).

A minimal change: have \`AbstractIndexingAdvice\` accept the service interface class in the subclass contract (either via constructor arg or via an abstract \`getServiceInterface()\` method), then at \`@PostConstruct\` reflect every name in \`TRIGGER_METHODS \\u222a PURGE_METHODS\` against \`serviceInterface.getMethods()\` and throw \`IllegalStateException\` if any don't resolve. Also assert \`PURGE_METHODS \\u2286 TRIGGER_METHODS\`.

Every consumer would get the safety for free at module startup, before any AOP invocation can silently miss.

## Failure mode prevented

A typo in \`TRIGGER_METHODS\` (e.g., \"saveBll\" instead of \"saveBill\") ships green, runs in production for weeks, and the failure surfaces only when ops notices the read store hasn't been updated. Bean-init validation turns this into a deterministic startup failure that's caught in CI on the first build.

Related: the billing slice's PR has the workaround test (\`IndexingAdviceConfigTest\`) that this issue would obviate.

title: Backend write durability: silent index drift when post-commit dispatch fails
body:
## Problem

`AbstractIndexingAdvice` serializes the entity synchronously inside the originating transaction, then dispatches the backend write asynchronously after commit (via the after-commit dispatcher mentioned in `AbstractRecordSerializer`'s ADR notes).

If the post-commit dispatch fails — Lucene I/O error, Elasticsearch unavailable, MySQL backend deadlock, dispatcher queue saturated — the transaction is already committed. The source-of-truth row is in the relational DB, the index has no record of the change, and there is:

- No retry
- No dead-letter queue
- No metric or alert
- No way for a consumer to know the index is stale relative to the DB

The drift is permanent until something else re-saves the entity (which fires the advice again) or a full reindex runs.

## Why this matters

This isn't a theoretical concern. A real production sequence:

1. Backend (ES / Lucene) has a transient I/O blip.
2. 50 bill saves in that window get committed to MySQL but never reach the index.
3. The blip resolves and indexing resumes for new saves.
4. The 50 affected bills are now silently missing from search results — possibly forever.

The index drifts ~5% from truth, and consumers building dashboards on top of it (cashier shift reports, refund approval queues, etc.) show stale numbers with no signal that anything is wrong.

## Suggested approaches

Several options, in increasing rigor:

1. **Failure metrics + structured log.** Emit a Micrometer counter (`querystore.index.write.failure` tagged by resource_type and backend) and a structured ERROR log with the resource UUID. Lets operators detect the drift, even if they can't auto-recover.

2. **Dead-letter queue + replay tool.** Persist failed writes to a `querystore_failed_writes` table with (resource_type, resource_uuid, payload, error, attempt_count, last_attempt_at). A scheduled job retries them with exponential backoff; an admin tool surfaces the queue.

3. **Configurable "fail closed" mode.** Per-resource-type option: synchronous backend write inside the transaction, blocking commit until the index write succeeds. Trades latency for consistency. Useful for resource types where staleness is unacceptable (financial bills?) and acceptable to skip for high-volume types (Obs?).

4. **Backend health probe.** Pre-flight check before each dispatch; if the backend reports unhealthy, fall back to the dead-letter path rather than attempting the write that will fail.

(1) is the minimum viable improvement and would catch most production drift in time to recover. (2) is the principled fix. (3) is a v2 capability. (4) is an optimization on (2).

## Failure mode prevented

Without this, the querystore's reliability ceiling is "as reliable as the backend, minus all unrecovered transient failures, with no way to know how much drift accumulated." That's a production data integrity gap.

Surfaced during a billing module slice that adds four resource types. The slice itself does nothing wrong — it relies on the SPI's promised at-least-once delivery — but in the absence of durability tooling, every consumer module silently inherits the same risk.

See https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-billing/pull/176 (the ADR) for context on what's being indexed.

title: AbstractIndexingAdvice: extension points needed for non-standard trigger surfaces
body:
## Context

Reporting from the [appointments module's querystore SPI contribution](https://github.com/dkayiwa/openmrs-module-appointments/compare/master...querystore-integration) (PR-ready against `Bahmni/openmrs-module-appointments`). I needed to write **two custom `AfterReturningAdvice` classes** alongside the one that extends `AbstractIndexingAdvice`, because the base class's contract is too restrictive for trigger surfaces that aren't one-entity-per-call.

Three sub-issues with the same root cause — the base class assumes the textbook case and forecloses on extension for everything else:

### 1. `afterReturning(...)` is `final` and catches only `RuntimeException`

Concrete failure mode I documented: a deployment lands a querystore version with a renamed SPI symbol (e.g. `ClinicalRecordSerializer.serialize` → something else) → `NoSuchMethodError` thrown from `dispatch()` → escapes the base's `catch (RuntimeException e)` → unwinds the AOP proxy to the clinical-thread save on `validateAndSave`/`changeStatus`/etc → user sees a phantom save failure even though the originating transaction committed.

I widened the catch to `RuntimeException | LinkageError` in my two custom advices but **cannot mirror the change in the advice that extends `AbstractIndexingAdvice`**, because `afterReturning` is `final`. The asymmetry is documented in the appointments module's class Javadoc as a known limitation that points back here.

### 2. `entityFrom(returnValue, args)` is `private final`

Can't be overridden. The `updateAppointmentProviderResponse(AppointmentProvider providerWithResponse)` case in my contribution needs to navigate `args[0].getAppointment()` to reach the affected `Appointment`. I had to write `AppointmentProviderResponseIndexingAdvice` from scratch as a direct `AfterReturningAdvice` implementation because the base's entity-extraction logic only handles `returnValue` or `args[0]` as `T` directly.

### 3. `collectTree(T root)` is typed `List<T>` on a single root type

Can't fan one `AppointmentRecurringPattern` into many `Appointment` documents from a subclass. `RecurringAppointmentIndexingAdvice` is also a direct `AfterReturningAdvice` because the base can't express "one root entity produces many indexable child entities of a different type."

## Suggested fix

Two paths, either of which would have let me write one advice class extending the base instead of three:

**Path A (least disruptive)**: keep `afterReturning` final but extract its body behind protected primitives — `protected void dispatch(T root)`, `protected T entityFrom(...)`, `protected List<? extends BaseOpenmrsData> collectTreeAs(Object root)` — and widen the catch in the existing final method to `RuntimeException | LinkageError`. Existing subclasses keep working; new subclasses can override any primitive.

**Path B (more flexibility, but a contract change)**: make `afterReturning` non-final, with the current implementation as the default. Subclasses override only when they need to.

Both paths benefit from also widening `indexer()` / `dispatcher()` from package-private to `protected` (see separate issue) so custom advices can reach the bridge beans without re-doing `Context.getRegisteredComponent` lookups.

## Backwards compatibility

Adding new protected primitives alongside the existing final method is fully backwards-compatible. Widening the existing `catch (RuntimeException e)` to `RuntimeException | LinkageError` is also backwards-compatible (catches a strict superset). Making methods non-final is technically a binary-compatibility regression for anyone who relied on the final marker, but in practice subclasses only override what they need.

## Empirical evidence

In the appointments contribution, the slice ended up with three advice classes (`AppointmentIndexingAdvice` extends the base; `RecurringAppointmentIndexingAdvice` and `AppointmentProviderResponseIndexingAdvice` don't). The two non-base ones each duplicate ~60 lines of dispatch skeleton that the base already implements. Closing this issue would let all three share one base.

Related: #16 (widen type bound) addresses a different rigidity in the same base class.

QueryDocument cross-cutting field contract has no enforcement; typos silently produce broken documents
body:
## Context

[qsADR-13](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-querystore/blob/main/docs/adr.md#decision-13-module-extension-spi-service-provider-interface-for-custom-resource-types) names the required cross-cutting fields every contributed document must carry: `patient_uuid`, `resource_type`, `resource_uuid`, `date`, `last_modified`, `text`, plus optional but expected `location_*`, `provider_*`, `encounter_*`, `visit_*`, `form_*`, `encounter_type_*`.

`QueryDocument` accepts any combination of set/unset:

```java
public QueryDocument serialize(Appointment a) {
    QueryDocument doc = new QueryDocument();
    doc.setResourceUuid(a.getUuid());        // set
    doc.setPatientUuid(...);                  // set
    // forgot to call doc.setResourceType(\"appointments_appointment\")
    // forgot to call doc.setLastModified(...)
    return doc;
}
```

This compiles. The document goes through the bridge pipeline, gets indexed, and ends up in the backend missing two of the five required cross-cutting fields. **No validation fires; no test catches it unless the test happens to assert the specific missing field.**

## Concrete failure modes

From my appointments contribution:
- A typo'd metadata key (e.g. `start_date_tiime`) silently produces a document missing the value. Consumers querying for `start_date_time` get empty results forever. I had to add explicit per-field assertions in `serializesFullyPopulatedAppointment` after catching one of these myself (round 6 of harden iterations).
- A dropped field after a refactor (e.g. someone deletes `doc.setResourceType(...)` thinking it's set automatically) silently produces non-routable documents.
- A null `last_modified` falls back to last-write-wins, breaking the qsADR-3 race guard for that document — concurrent AOP and bootstrap writes silently lose to whichever fires last.

All three are silent-failure-mode bugs per the \"silent corruption is harder to detect than a crash\" rule. CI doesn't catch them; users see wrong query results weeks later.

## Suggested fix

Two complementary options:

1. **`QueryDocument.validate()` method called by the bridge pipeline** before upsert. Throws if any required cross-cutting field is unset. The bridge already catches `RuntimeException` (per ADR Decision 12), so the failure is logged at warn level and the bad document is skipped — but unlike today's silent corruption, the operator now sees the failure in logs.

2. **`QueryDocument.Builder` API** that requires the cross-cutting fields up front:

```java
QueryDocument doc = QueryDocument.builder()
    .resourceType(\"appointments_appointment\")     // required, compile-time
    .resourceUuid(a.getUuid())                    // required
    .patientUuid(p.getUuid())                     // required
    .lastModified(Instant.now())                  // required
    .date(LocalDate.now())                        // required
    .text(\"...\")                                  // required
    .metadata(\"appointment_number\", \"APPT-001\")    // optional, fluent
    .build();
```

Builder catches the bug at compile time for documents constructed via the builder; `validate()` catches it for documents constructed via the legacy setter API. Both can ship together.

## Backwards compatibility

`validate()` is additive — existing serializers that already populate all required fields keep working. Adding a `Builder` is additive — existing setter-based serializers keep working until they're migrated.

## Empirical evidence

In the appointments contribution, I added per-metadata-key assertions in `serializesFullyPopulatedAppointment` only after multiple harden iterations caught me missing keys (5 keys were unasserted at one point — `location_name`, `appointment_service_name`, `appointment_service_type_name`, `start_date_time`, `end_date_time`). Every contributor will hit the same trap. The validation belongs upstream so each contributor doesn't reinvent the assertion discipline.
